2. **Nonfatal — `thm-abelianisation-of-a-free-group-is-free-abelian`, proof step 1.2 and its contract input map.** [Step 1.2](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-abelianisation-of-a-free-group-is-free-abelian.md:50) calculates that \(f\) kills each individual commutator and immediately concludes
   \([F(X),F(X)]\subseteq\ker f\), citing only `[given]`. The needed fact is that the commutator subgroup is the subgroup **generated** by all commutators; the dependency states exactly:
   “The commutator subgroup … is the subgroup generated by all commutators” and
   \([G,G]=\langle\{[g,h]\}\rangle\) ([dependency text](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-commutator-and-commutator-subgroup.md:36)). The [contract](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/freegroups-1-proof-contracts.json:1607) records only “given hypotheses and direct calculation,” omitting that generated-subgroup input. The inference is correct and repairable in well under 30 seconds by adding the exact commutator-subgroup Fact, so I assess it nonfatal.

3. **Nonfatal — proof-contract boundary records are not anchored to the proofs.** In the merged [proof contract](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/research/freegroups-1-proof-contracts.json:1645), boundary evidence repeatedly begins with the meaningless fourfold prefix “Statement and proof.” More concretely:

   - The abelianisation contract says “The one-generator case is infinite cyclic” at line 1659, but the item never states or proves that claim.
   - The preservation proposition’s contract says “Zero moves change nothing” at line 1758, although its Statement concerns one elementary transformation and its proof has no zero-move case.
   - Its “Renaming uses a fresh symbol” entry at line 1768 does not describe the arbitrary-bijection renaming proof.
   - Several Tietze-theorem entries at lines 1903–1920 claim empty/trivial cases are expressly handled when the proof only covers them implicitly through the general finite construction.

   These do not refute the mathematics, but they fail the required anchored-boundary contract and should be replaced by actual proof locations or honest `not_applicable` dispositions.

For the hard Tietze theorem I checked both iff directions, \(X=\varnothing\), \(Y=\varnothing\), empty relator sets, trivial presented groups, overlapping alphabets, and the zero-move case. Both constructions reach the literal same presentation
\[
\mathcal C=\langle X\cup Y\mid R\cup S\cup\{d_x\}\cup\{d_y\}\rangle.
\]
All indexing sets are finite, so the construction is a genuinely finite sequence and every intermediate presentation is finite. Reversing the \(\mathcal Q\to\mathcal C\) sequence leaves the forcing relators in place and removes every occurrence of a dictionary generator before deleting it.

I independently agree that the earlier overlapping-alphabet omission in `def-tietze-transformations` was nonfatal under the 30-second rule. The current fresh finite alphabet \(Z\), factoring \(X\to Z\to Y\), closes it correctly.

The abelianisation proof body correctly establishes that the quotient is abelian, factors maps in the direction
\[
F(X)\xrightarrow q F(X)^{\mathrm{ab}}\longrightarrow A,
\]
and proves extension and uniqueness for the map \(q\circ\iota:X\to F(X)^{\mathrm{ab}}\). Thus it establishes the free-object/basis universal property and does not merely assert an identification with \(\mathbb Z^n\).
